news.title: FIFA President Infantino To Attend U-20 Women's World Cup Opener In Katowice
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino will make his first public appearance at the Under-20 Women's World Cup in Katowice following the controversial abandonment of his $20 billion World Cup commercial rights sale proposal. FIFA President Gianni Infantino will attend the opening match of the Under-20 Women's World Cup in Katowice on Saturday, the first tournament organised by world football's ruling body since his abandoned proposal to sell a stake in the World Cup. The Swiss administrator called off the plan, which valued the commercial rights of the World Cup and other FIFA tournaments at $20 billion, in late July in the face of a fierce backlash from regional governing bodies including Europe's UEFA and major stakeholders in the sport. A spokesperson for the Polish Football Association confirmed the embattled Infantino would be at the opening game.

news.title: Gianni Infantino to attend FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup opener in Poland
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino will attend the opening match of the FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup in Katowice, Poland, on Saturday, September 5. The Polish Football Association has confirmed his presence for the game between hosts Poland and Argentina.Poland have been drawn in Group A alongside Argentina, Mexico and Benin. They will face Mexico on September 8 before finishing their group campaign against Benin on September 11. The 2026 tournament is the 12th edition of the FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup and will feature 24 teams.

news.title: Infantino Set for U-20 Women’s World Cup Opener Amid FIFA Controversy
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino will be in the spotlight when the U-20 Women’s World Cup gets underway in Poland on Saturday, just weeks after he was forced to abandon a controversial proposal involving the commercial rights to FIFA’s biggest tournaments. Infantino is expected to attend the opening match in Katowice, where Poland will face Argentina, as the world football governing body begins another edition of its youth women’s competition. A spokesperson for the Polish Football Association confirmed the FIFA president’s attendance, with about 15,000 spectators expected for the first two matches of the tournament. news.title: Steve Clarke needed to give SFA 'a little shove' for new contract
news.lede: Steve Clarke sensed the players needed freshness in the dressing room. Former Scotland boss Steve Clarke says he had to cajole the Scottish FA into handing him a new contract as national head coach shortly before the World Cup finals this summer because he felt the governing body was hedging its bets. But the 63-year-old insists he nevertheless always planned to resign if he failed to lead Scotland beyond the group stage for the first time. Speaking for the first time since the tournament in the Americas, Clarke was being interviewed by former Chelsea and Scotland team-mate Pat Nevin at Spartans Community Foundation dinner in Edinburgh.

news.title: Africa’s football progress key to future support for Infantino
news.lede: African football officials are prioritising development over governance disputes surrounding FIFA President Gianni Infantino and the continent’s progress will guide future leadership decisions, said Benin Football Federation President Marcellin ​Bocove. Bocove was speaking ahead of the FIFA under-20 Women’s World Cup, which runs from Saturday ‌through September 27 in Poland. The tournament is the first global FIFA competition since the governance row triggered by Infantino’s proposal to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors. news.title: FIFA's Infantino Attends Under-20 Women's World Cup Amid Controversy
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino will be present at the opening match of the Under-20 Women's World Cup in Katowice this Saturday. This marks the first major tournament organized by FIFA since Infantino's controversial proposal to sell World Cup stakes was abandoned. The proposal, which valued the commercial rights of FIFA tournaments at $20 billion, faced strong opposition from regional governing bodies, including UEFA and key stakeholders, leading to its withdrawal in late July. Nevertheless, a Polish Football Association spokesperson confirmed Infantino's attendance at the opening game.
